outcome: I can make a prediction or promise using regular and irregular future forms.
explanation: Futur simple presents future events, predictions and commitments. Add -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont to a regular -er or -ir verb, removing the last e from an -re verb. Irregular stems include ser- (be), aur- (have), ir- (go), fer- (do), viendr- (come), prendr- (take) and pourr- (be able). After quand (when) or dès que (as soon as), French uses a future form for future reference, even where English uses a present form. Contrast je partirai (I will leave) with je partirais (I would leave).

For an imagined condition, use si plus imparfait, then conditional: si j'avais le temps, je viendrais means if I had time, I would come. Do not put the conditional after si in this pattern.

A clear request identifies the help needed and any deadline. In a work or education setting, use vous with an unfamiliar professional and check that you have understood the proposed solution.

outcome: I can organize a short opinion paragraph or presentation with a summary.
explanation: A structured response leads a reader from a claim to support and a conclusion. Start with a clear opinion, add a reason and a relevant example, then restate the implication rather than copying the opening. D'abord (first), par exemple (for example) and en conclusion (in conclusion) can mark these roles. When summarizing another speaker, separate their main point from your own view. For speaking practice, read a short argument to a partner and ask them to summarize it before replying.
